subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through Acme Retail's recommendation use case today. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist of models to evaluate based on the constraints you shared (short responses for product recommendations, heavy throughput at peak, and strict latency targets for UI):

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Typical prompt length: 50–120 tokens (mostly product attributes + user context)
- Response length: 40–100 tokens (short recommendations + 1–2 bullets)
- Peak QPS target: ~120 rps across your cluster; burst to 250 rps for seasonal spikes
- Latency target (p95): <200ms for UI-critical interactions
- Cost sensitivity: want to optimize for per-request cost without regressing quality more than ~3% on NPS-style evaluations

Recommended shortlist (ranked for evaluation):
1) redwood-rev2-13b-8bit (balanced) — Best baseline for cost vs. quality. Expected median latency ~90–130ms on our Dedicated 4xA10 config; good at short-form prompts and supports batching. Per-token cost estimate: low-mid.
2) gptx-mini-7b-quant (low-cost/high-throughput) — Excellent for throughput and cost; slightly lower quality for nuanced product personalization but often indistinguishable on short prompts. Expected median latency ~60–100ms. Per-token cost: low.
3) llama2-70b-16bit (high-quality/fallback) — Highest quality for edge-case personalization and long-tail prompts. Higher latency (~220–320ms) and cost; recommend as a canary/fallback for critical paths only.

Rationale (cost / latency / quality tradeoffs):
- redwood-rev2-13b-8bit: sweet spot for many recommendation flows — keeps p95 comfortably under 200ms with batching and KV prefix caching; small quality delta vs the 70B on short prompts but ~40–60% lower cost.
- gptx-mini-7b-quant: pick this if your real-time stack prioritizes throughput and cost; expect better headroom for spikes with autoscaling and cheaper reserved capacity.
- llama2-70b: only for the small percentage of requests that require deep personalization or multi-turn history; use as a conditional fallback or for offline ranking.

Attached: acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (shortlist + notes), latency_benchmarks.pdf (our measured p50/p95 on similar workloads), eval_prompt_set.json (recommended prompt set we propose you run for a 2-week eval).

Next steps we suggest:
- You confirm which two models you want in a 2-week A/B eval (we typically recommend one balanced + one low-cost).
- We drop in the eval_prompt_set.json and run baseline quality + latency runs; share live dashboards and per-prompt regression alerts.
- Quick sync next week to finalize telemetry and SLA expectations; Vivek will lead the technical onboarding.

Can you confirm which two models you'd like to start with? Also let us know any additional guardrails (e.g., hard latency cutoff, disallowed tokens, or redlines).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick questions before we lock in the eval:
- For short-form recommendations, which of the three do you expect to hit <200ms p95 out-of-the-box on a hosted Dedicated pool?
- Can you provide a rough per-request cost estimate for the 40–80 token responses (including inference + reserved overhead) for the two lower-cost options?

We want to aim for the redwood-rev2-13b + gptx-mini-7b split if that makes sense — rev2 as baseline, mini as the cost-optimized variant. If those numbers look reasonable, we'll sign off to start the 2-week eval and schedule the technical kickoff.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of Product, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme-retail.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Alex — forwarding some ballpark numbers and links so you can share internally. These are empirical estimates from similar retail workloads on our Dedicated 4xA10 profile. Final numbers will vary by sequence length and batching config; we'll instrument during the eval and publish a per-route cost breakdown.

Estimated latency (median / p95) and cost (per 40–80 token response):
- redwood-rev2-13b-8bit: median 95ms / p95 160–190ms; estimated cost $0.012–$0.018 per response (includes reserved capacity amortization).
- gptx-mini-7b-quant: median 70ms / p95 120–150ms; estimated cost $0.006–$0.010 per response.
- llama2-70b-16bit: median 240ms / p95 320–400ms; estimated cost $0.045–$0.075 per response.

Links:
- Benchmark PDF: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=1a2b3c_acme-model-shortlist (latency_benchmarks.pdf)
- Eval prompt set: https://drive.redwood.ai/open?id=2b3c4d_eval-prompt-set (eval_prompt_set.json)
- Live dashboard (we'll create during eval): https://dash.redwood.ai/acme/ACME-2026-42

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for product-context prompts to shave ~10–30% off p95 depending on cache hit rate.
- For spikes, configure a burst policy to fall back to the gptx-mini-7b variant at 80% pool utilization to preserve p95 targets while controlling cost.
- We will instrument quality checks tied to your NPS-style prompt set and alert if quality regresses >3% against baseline.

If that looks good I can have engineering spin up the eval configs once we get your sign-off.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
